newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee futures called down 1.00 to 1.50 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee futures called down 1.00 to 1.50 cents.

text.p: CSCE arabica coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 1.50 cents lower Monday on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, traders said.
LIFFE robusta coffee futures turned lower after a firm start. Most-active March delivery fell $20 to $1,300 a tonne by the midday break, while spot January off $5 at $1,340.
Friday, New York arabica futures ended firmer in choppy dealings, with March delivery up 0.25 cent at 119.60 cents a lb, a fresh seven-month high, after ranging 120.80 to 118.50.
Second-position May also ended 0.25 cent higher at 117.40 cents, while the outer months finished up 0.50 to 0.80.
On the charts, traders pegged March support at 117.75-117.50, then 115.00. Resistance was seen at 121.50, with the next upside hurdle put near 124.00 cents.

In fundamental news, Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters (Febec) said late Friday the country exported 1.53 million 60-kg bags of coffee, ground and in beans, in December, below an upwardly revised November figure of 1.63 million bags.
The December total is double the 783,701 bags exported in the same month in 1995. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212 859 1640))
